prerequisites: Basic knowledge of mechanical principles, establishing equations of motion, vibration engineering, and measurement technology.
Basic knowledge of mathematics: solving differential equations, series expansion (Taylor, Fourier), matrix calculus, calculations with complex numbers.
Understanding schematic diagrams of mechanical systems, sufficient practice in applying prior knowledge from mathematics and mechanics.
Mechanics 2 module and successful completion of the StEOP (Study Entrance and Orientation Phase).

learning_outcomes.text: Acquisition of the ability to form problem- and effort-adapted models for treating dynamic problems in real machines.
Acquisition of analytical and numerical skills for treating model-motion equations.
Ability to interpret measured phenomena in machines by comparison with numerical results.
Calculation of the degree of non-uniformity and inertial forces as well as the realization of mass balancing of mechanisms.
Modeling and dynamic analysis of belt and gear drives, simple calculations on rotor systems.
Communication when working on problems in a team, discussion and presentation of results and proposed solutions.
formulate mechanical models for dynamic problems in real machines in a problem- and effort-adapted manner.
safely apply analytical and numerical methods for treating model-motion equations.
systematically investigate measured phenomena in machines by comparing them with numerical results.
correctly calculate the degree of non-uniformity and inertial forces in mechanisms.
methodically perform mass balancing in mechanisms.
dynamically and model-based investigate belt and gear drives.
design block foundations for machine installation.
correctly calculate fundamental parameters of rotor systems.
structure solution paths cooperatively and considering time constraints.
constructively discuss problems, intermediate results, and assumptions in a team.
present results and proposed solutions in a team in a structured and audience-appropriate manner.
discuss the applicability of mechanical models as well as analytical and numerical methods considering environmental and work-related conditions.
implement modifications and improvements to their own solution strategies considering peer feedback.

syllabus_topics: Fundamentals of modeling in technical dynamics
Equations of motion and constraint forces of EFG mechanisms (circular cam drives, crank drives, etc.)
Degree of non-uniformity, inertial forces, and mass balancing of mechanisms
Design of block foundations for machine installation
Deepening into torsional vibratory systems (belt and gear drives)
Fundamentals of bending vibrations of shafts and rotors
teaching_methods: Lecture with media support on theoretical foundations
Practice of learned material by independently solving tasks, partly in teams and under instructor guidance
